disclosure.h1: Before we shop this for you.
disclosure.sub: One thing to agree to, then the questions.
disclosure.plain: What that means, in plain terms
disclosure.p1:
We are an independent agency, not an insurance company. To find you
            a price we send what you tell us to several carriers at once, and
            each of them looks up the same public records any insurer would —
            your driving record, past claims and prior coverage — to work out
            what they can offer you.
disclosure.p2: We use it to quote your insurance and nothing else. We do not sell your information, and the only people who contact you are licensed Safe House agents. Our Privacy Policy covers how it is handled and how long it is kept.
disclosure.p3:
Nothing is bound and nothing is charged on this page. Every price
            you see is subject to verification before a policy can be issued.
disclosure.agreeLead: I have read and agree to the above disclosure.

cov.g1Why: What your policy pays when a crash is your fault. Every state requires some of this, and it pays nothing toward your own car.
cov.liabHint: Injuries per person / per accident, then their property — in thousands.
cov.umbiHint: Pays your injuries when the driver who hit you has no insurance, or not enough.
cov.umpdHint: The same idea for your car, with a $250 deductible.
cov.g2: Medical bills for you and your passengers
cov.g2Why: Pays for the people in your car, whoever caused the crash. Pick one of the two — a vehicle cannot carry both.
cov.medpayHint: No deductible. Pays alongside your health insurance.
cov.pipHint: Broader — can also pay lost wages.
cov.mpWarn: A vehicle may have Medical Payments or Personal Injury Protection, not both.
cov.fullQMany: Comprehensive and collision on this vehicle?
cov.fullQOne: Comprehensive and collision on your vehicle?
cov.fullHint: Liability only is cheaper, but nothing then pays to fix this car. A car with a loan on it almost always has to carry both.
cov.dcompHint: Hail, theft, fire, glass, an animal.
cov.dcollHint: You hit something, whoever was at fault.
cov.rentalHint: What it pays a day toward a hire car while this one is being repaired.
cov.roadsideHint: Towing, jump start, fuel, a flat changed — what it pays per breakdown.
cov.trip: Add trip interruption — help with lodging, meals and getting home when the breakdown happens far from it. Not priced online: your agent arranges this with the carrier you pick, so the prices you see next will not include it.
cov.g3WhyMany: Priced separately for each vehicle, so the financed one and the paid-off one do not have to carry the same thing.
cov.g3WhyOne: None of the above pays to fix your own car. This is the part that does.
cov.cslNote: A combined single limit covers injury and property together, so uninsured-motorist cover is capped at that one figure rather than at a separate property-damage number.

um.why: Some options are greyed out — here is why
um.p: Uninsured motorist coverage pays when the driver who hits you cannot. Carriers will not write more of it than the liability underneath it, so with {liab} selected above, {rest}
um.many: the higher limits are not available yet.
um.one: the higher limits on {cov} are not available yet.
um.next: Nothing is broken — raise your liability limit to {next} or higher and those options open up. Not sure? Your agent will go through it with you.
um.raise: Nothing is broken. Raise your liability limit above and those options open up.

tip.liab: What your policy pays for the harm you cause to other people. The first two numbers are injuries — one person, then everyone in the crash — and the third is their car and anything else you damage, all in thousands. It pays nothing toward your own car. A combined single limit (CSL) is one pot for all three instead.
tip.umbi: Pays your injuries when the driver who hit you has no insurance, or not enough of it, or drove off. Texas and New Mexico both require carriers to offer it, and turning it down has to be in writing.
tip.umpd: The same idea for your car rather than your body — it pays to repair it when the at-fault driver cannot. The $250 deductible is what you pay before it starts.
tip.medpay: Medical bills for you and your passengers after a crash, no matter who caused it and with no deductible. It pays alongside your health insurance and can cover what that leaves behind.
tip.pip: Broader than Medical Payments: as well as medical bills it can pay lost wages and the cost of someone to help at home while you recover. A vehicle carries this or Medical Payments, not both.
tip.dcomp: Comprehensive is damage that is not a collision — hail, theft, fire, a cracked windscreen, hitting a deer. The deductible is what you pay yourself before the carrier pays: a $500 deductible on $3,000 of hail means you pay $500. A lower deductible costs more every month.
tip.dcoll: Collision is your own car after hitting something — another vehicle, a kerb, a wall — whoever was at fault. The deductible works the same way, and it applies each time you claim, not once a year.
tip.rental: Pays for a hire car while yours is being repaired after a covered claim. The figure is what it pays a day — pick one close to what a rental actually costs here, because the difference comes out of your pocket. How many days it keeps paying is set by the carrier.
tip.roadside: Towing, winching, a jump start, fuel, a locksmith, a flat tyre changed and on-scene labour. The figure is what it pays per breakdown — a tow across El Paso is usually under $100, one off the interstate can be more.
tip.hUnits: How many separate homes share this building. A normal house is 1. A duplex is 2 — even if you only own or live in one side.
tip.hStories: Floors of living space, not counting a basement or an attic you cannot stand up in. A one-storey house with a loft is 1.5.
tip.hSqft: The heated and cooled living space. Garages, porches and unfinished basements are normally left out. An estimate is fine.
tip.hBaths: Count a half bath — a toilet and sink with no shower or tub — as 0.5.
tip.hYear: The year the house was originally built, not the year you bought it or last remodelled it.
tip.hPrimary: Whether you live here most of the year. A second home, a rental you own or a holiday place is a different kind of policy.
tip.hNew: Built within roughly the last year and never lived in. Most carriers give a discount for it.
tip.hConstr: What holds the house up — the frame behind the walls, not what you see from the street. If the outside is brick over a wooden frame, that is masonry veneer.
tip.hFound: What the house sits on. Slab is a concrete pad straight on the ground and is the most common in Texas and New Mexico.
tip.hSiding: What you actually see on the outside walls.
tip.hRoofYr: When the roof covering was last replaced, not the year the house was built. This is the single biggest thing on a home quote here — if you are unsure, your best estimate is better than leaving it.
tip.hRoofSlope: How steep it is. Low is a gentle pitch you could nearly walk up, steep is one you clearly could not. Not sure is fine.
tip.hWh: Where the tank is. It matters because of what a leak would reach — a heater above living space can cause far more damage than one in a garage.
tip.hEff: The day you want cover to begin. If you are buying, this is normally your closing date.
tip.hGar: Built-in or attached means it shares a wall with the house. Detached is a separate building.
tip.mEndorse: The motorcycle authorisation on your driver licence — in Texas the "M" endorsement. It is what makes it legal to ride on public roads, and it is separate from the licence itself. If you are not sure, look for an M next to the class on the front of your licence.
tip.mCourse: A rider course approved by the state — the Basic RiderCourse and similar. Finishing one can qualify you for a discount with several insurance companies, so it is worth saying if you have.
tip.mExp: How long you have been riding on a public road, not how long you have owned this particular motorcycle.
tip.mFreq: Roughly how often you ride in the months you actually ride. Nobody is holding you to it — it is used to work out how much the bike is used.
tip.mCC: Engine size, printed in the bike’s handbook and usually in its name — a Sportster 1200 is 1200cc. It is one of the biggest things in a motorcycle price.
tip.mAbs: Brakes that stop the wheels locking up in a hard stop. Most bikes made in the last ten years have them, and many carriers discount for it.
tip.mTrike: Three wheels rather than two — a factory trike or a conversion. It is rated differently, so it matters.
tip.mMod: Anything changed from how the factory built it that affects how it runs or what it is worth — a different frame, a turbo or nitrous kit, a big-bore kit, a lift. Cosmetic parts go under accessory coverage instead.
tip.mLien: The bank or finance company that holds the loan on the bike. They normally have to be named on the policy.
tip.mAddl: Anyone else with a financial interest who needs to be told about the policy — a lessor, or a co-owner.
tip.mFiling: A form an insurance company files with the state to prove you are insured, usually after a licence suspension. If you have been told you need an SR-22, say so here — not every carrier will file one.
tip.mAssoc: Some carriers discount for membership of a riding association. If yours is not listed, pick Other and tell us at the end.

liabilityLimits.title: How much liability coverage would you like?
liabilityLimits.why: This coverage helps pay for injuries or property damage you cause to others in an accident.
liabilityLimits.tip: The first two numbers are the injury limits — per person, then per accident — and the last is property damage, all in thousands. "CSL" is a combined single limit: one pot of money covering both. Higher limits generally provide more protection.

umBodilyInjuryLimits.title: Uninsured or underinsured driver — injuries
umBodilyInjuryLimits.why: Helps protect you and your passengers if you are injured by a driver who does not have insurance, or does not have enough of it.
umBodilyInjuryLimits.tip: On a motorcycle this is the coverage riders most often wish they had bought. In Texas a carrier has to offer it and you have to turn it down in writing.

umPropertyDamage.title: Uninsured or underinsured driver — your motorcycle
umPropertyDamage.why: Helps pay for damage to your motorcycle caused by an uninsured or underinsured driver, subject to the applicable deductible.

pipLimit.title: Personal injury protection
pipLimit.why: Can help pay certain medical expenses and other covered costs after an accident, regardless of who was at fault.

medicalPayments.title: Medical payments
medicalPayments.why: Helps pay eligible medical expenses for you and your passengers after a covered accident.

physicalDamageValuation.title: How would you like your motorcycle protected?
physicalDamageValuation.why: This decides what happens to the bike itself if it is stolen, damaged or written off.

d.none-liability-only: Your motorcycle itself would not have comprehensive or collision coverage.
d.actual-cash-value: If your motorcycle is totalled, the insurance company generally pays its value at the time of the loss, taking age and condition into consideration.
d.agreed-value: You and the insurance company agree a value for the motorcycle up front, including eligible accessory coverage. May need photos, receipts, title or an inspection.
d.total-loss-coverage: For eligible newer motorcycles, may pay based on the MSRP of a current model-year motorcycle of the same make and model after a covered total loss.

comprehensiveDeductible.title: Comprehensive deductible
comprehensiveDeductible.why: Comprehensive generally covers theft, vandalism, weather, fire and certain other losses that are not a collision.
comprehensiveDeductible.tip: The deductible is what you pay yourself before the insurance pays the rest. A higher one lowers the premium and costs you more if you do claim.

collisionDeductible.title: Collision deductible
collisionDeductible.why: Collision helps pay for damage to your motorcycle from a covered collision.

roadsideOption.title: Roadside assistance
roadsideOption.why: For when the bike will not go — towing to a repair shop, winching, a jump start or fuel brought out to you.
roadsideOption.tip: Trip interruption adds help with lodging, food and getting around if a covered breakdown happens far from home — usually more than 100 miles away. What it pays varies by insurance company, and your agent will tell you what the quoting carrier includes.

d.roadside: Towing, winching, jump starts and fuel delivery.
d.roadside-w-trip-interruption: Roadside assistance plus help with lodging, food and transport when a covered breakdown happens far from home.

carriedContentsLimit.title: Personal belongings you carry
carriedContentsLimit.why: Helps cover things like a phone, touring gear or camping kit if they are damaged in a covered comprehensive or collision loss.

accessoryCoverageRange.title: Accessory coverage
accessoryCoverageRange.why: Covers eligible equipment and modifications that did not come from the manufacturer — custom paint, chrome, exhaust, electronics, a sidecar or a motorcycle trailer.

safetyApparelCoverage.title: Riding gear
safetyApparelCoverage.why: Covers eligible motorcycle safety apparel and riding equipment — helmet, jacket, gloves, boots.

transportTrailer.title: A trailer you haul the bike on?
transportTrailer.why: A trailer used to transport the motorcycle, not one you tow behind it.

disappearingDeductible.title: Disappearing deductible
disappearingDeductible.why: On some carriers your deductible shrinks for every year you ride without a claim. Availability depends on the insurance company.

bikes.sub:
The VIN is what gets you a price on screen. Without it an agent
        has to look the bike up and call you back.

riders.sub:
Everyone in the household who rides, plus anyone else who
        should be listed.

riding.sub:
Experience and a safety course are two of the few things that
        reliably bring a motorcycle premium down.

incidents.sub:
In the last five years, on any vehicle — not just a
        motorcycle. Carriers check anyway, and a surprise later is what changes a
        price after you have already been quoted.

history.prior: Have you had motorcycle insurance in the last 12 months?
history.assoc: Are you a member of a riding association?
history.res: What best describes where you live?
history.paperless: Happy to get your documents by email?
history.paperlessSub:
Policy documents and notices, sent
          electronically instead of by post. Several carriers discount for it.

covPolicy.sub:
These apply to the whole policy. Not sure? Pick what sounds
        right — your agent goes through it with you before anything is issued.

covBike.sub:
This is the big one, and it is set per motorcycle — an
        older bike and a new one rarely want the same answer.

covExtras.sub:
All optional. Skip anything you do not want — none is a
        perfectly good answer.

covSummary.sub: Change anything you want before we send it out.

contact.sub: We need a way to reach you before anything can be bound.
contact.smsLinks: See our SMS Terms and Privacy Policy.
contact.smsNote: Optional — you will get your quote either way.
contact.free: Free and no obligation. A licensed agent reviews everything before any policy is issued — nothing is bound on this page.

rating.msg: Sending your details to the carriers we represent…
rating.who: Real carriers, real rates — this can take a minute or two.

results.sub:
One price per company, lowest first. Most are six-month policies
        — any that covers a different length is marked and grouped on its own.
results.warnH: Two of these prices are not quite what you asked for
results.warnP:
Everything else is as you chose it. Your agent can price the rest properly
           when they call — nothing here is final.
results.personH: A person still has to look at these.
results.personP:
Online rating only applies the discounts the system can see by itself. It
            regularly misses ones you qualify for — how long you have been insured,
            paying in full or going paperless, a defensive driving course, another policy
            with the same company, good student, military, homeowner. A licensed Safe House
            agent goes through your quote by hand before anything is bought, and the price
            more often goes down than up.
results.dontClose: So if something below looks higher than you expected, do not close the tab. That is exactly what the call is for — and it costs you nothing.
results.note1:
Prices are based on the information you provided and are subject to
        verification of your driving history.
results.note2:
An agent will text or
        call you shortly to confirm every discount was applied — and to check whether you qualify for more.

confirm.sub: Nothing is charged here and no policy starts yet.
confirm.notFinal: This price is not final yet.
confirm.p:
A licensed Safe House agent will text or call you shortly to apply every discount you
          qualify for and to run your driving record. Your final price can change once that is done
          — most often it goes down.

picked.p: We sent your quote to your email and an agent is picking it up now.
picked.phone:
Keep your phone handy —
        an agent will text or call you shortly to confirm discounts and finish your quote.

done.p:
A licensed Safe House agent will get back to you with real options — in English or Spanish.
         If you would rather not wait, call us.
done.diag: Diagnostic · not shown on the live site

trust.p:
We use what you send only to prepare your quote. The only people who contact you are licensed
       Safe House agents — we do not sell your details or hand your number to anyone else.
